# The control panel: `_quarto.yml` {#sec-yml}

This one file is the table of contents, the theme, and the settings. Get
comfortable here and the rest of Quarto is just writing.

## A minimal book

```yaml
project:
  type: book
  output-dir: docs          # where the finished website is written

book:
  title: "My Course Book"
  author: "Your Name, Utrecht University"
  chapters:
    - index.qmd             # the front page
    - part: "Getting started"     # groups chapters under a heading
      chapters:
        - 01-writing.qmd
        - 02-figures.qmd
    - part: "Practicals"
      chapters:
        - 03-practical.qmd
  appendices:               # lettered instead of numbered
    - answers.qmd

format:
  html:
    theme: cosmo            # any Bootswatch theme
    toc: true
  pdf:
    documentclass: scrreprt # delete if you never want a PDF
```

Three blocks matter:

- **`project`** — what you are building, and where the output goes.
- **`book`** — the structure, and which chapters in which order.
- **`format`** — how each output type looks.

::: {.callout-important}
## The mistake everyone makes once
**A chapter that is not listed under `chapters:` does not exist.** Creating
`week3.qmd` is not enough — Quarto will render the book without it and give you
no warning at all. If a chapter is missing from the website, this is why, nine
times out of ten.
:::

::: {.screenshot}
`_quarto.yml` open in the editor with the `project` / `book` / `format` blocks
highlighted, next to the rendered sidebar, so the mapping is obvious.
:::

## Controlling the sidebar labels

A long chapter title makes an ugly sidebar entry. Give the sidebar its own
shorter text:

```yaml
    chapters:
      - text: "Introduction"
        href: Modellen/intro_modellen.qmd
```

Chapters can live in subfolders, as this example shows. Paths in `_quarto.yml`
are relative to the top of the project.

## Indentation

YAML indentation is meaningful, and must be **spaces, never tabs**. If Quarto
complains about the file and the message makes no sense, an indentation slip is
almost always the cause. RStudio inserts spaces for you if you leave its
defaults alone.

## Making it look like Utrecht University {#sec-theming}

Start from a [Bootswatch theme](https://bootswatch.com/) — `cosmo`, `flatly`
and `litera` all read well as a textbook — and layer your own SCSS on top:

```yaml
format:
  html:
    theme: [cosmo, uu.scss]
```

That is what this book uses, and the single entry is deliberate. Quarto will
happily give you a light/dark pair with a toggle in the corner:

```yaml
    theme:
      light: [cosmo, uu.scss]
      dark:  [darkly, uu-dark.scss]
```

The theme listed first is the default, and the reader's choice is remembered in
their browser. Add `respect-user-color-scheme: true` and it follows their
operating system instead.

::: {.callout-note}
## Why this book has no dark mode
The UU identity is specified on a white ground: red and yellow are defined
against paper, and yellow in particular becomes a different colour entirely on
a dark surface. A dark palette would be something we invented, not something
the university sanctioned — so this book stays light for every reader. Your own
book can decide differently; the mechanism is right there above.
:::

An SCSS file has two blocks. The `defaults` block sets variables *before*
Bootstrap is compiled; the `rules` block is ordinary CSS applied afterwards.

```scss
/*-- scss:defaults --*/
$uu-yellow: #FFCD00;    // UU geel — our most distinctive colour
$uu-red:    #C00A35;    // UU rood
$primary:   $uu-red !default;
$font-family-sans-serif: "Open Sans", Arial, sans-serif !default;
$headings-font-family:   "Merriweather", Georgia, serif !default;
$font-size-root: 17px !default;

/*-- scss:rules --*/
h2 { border-bottom: 2px solid $uu-yellow; }
```

The full [UU colour palette](https://www.uu.nl/en/organisation/corporate-identity/brand-policy/colour) is:

| Name | Hex | | Name | Hex |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| UU geel | `#FFCD00` | | UU groen | `#24A793` |
| UU rood | `#C00A35` | | UU blauw | `#5287C6` |
| UU creme | `#FFE6AB` | | UU donkerblauw | `#001240` |
| UU oranje | `#F3965E` | | UU paars | `#5B2182` |
| UU bordeauxrood | `#AA1555` | | UU bruin | `#6E3B23` |

: Utrecht University house-style colours. {#tbl-uu-colours}

The [UU standard fonts](https://www.uu.nl/en/organisation/corporate-identity/brand-policy/fonts)
are **Merriweather** and **Open Sans** (with **Zilla Slab** permitted for
headlines). All three are on Google Fonts, so a book can use them directly.
Link them in the page header:

```yaml
format:
  html:
    include-in-header:
      - text: |
          <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Merriweather:wght@300;400;700&family=Open+Sans:wght@400;600;700&display=swap">
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## Steal this book's theme
`uu.scss` in this project is a complete, commented UU house-style theme — the
palette, the fonts, callouts mapped onto the supporting colours, and the yellow
accent rules. Copy that one file plus the `theme:` and `include-in-header:`
blocks from this book's `_quarto.yml` into yours, and you are done.

There is a starting point for a dark variant in `_archive/uu-dark.scss` if you
decide your book wants one.
:::

::: {.callout-caution collapse="true"}
## A note on using yellow
UU yellow is a signature colour but a poor text colour — it fails contrast
requirements on white. Use it the way the university does: as an accent rule,
an underline, a highlight, a block of background. Keep body text and links in
red, black or dark blue.
:::

The same chapter side by side in light and dark mode, and the `uu.scss` file
showing the `$primary` colour change.
:::

## Useful extras

```yaml
book:
  favicon: figures/favicon.png
  search: true
  sidebar:
    logo: figures/uu-logo.png
    style: floating
    collapse-level: 1
    pinned: true
  page-footer:
    left: "Utrecht University"
    right: "Made with <a href='https://quarto.org/'>Quarto</a>"

format:
  html:
    toc-location: right
    lightbox: true            # click any figure to enlarge it
    code-overflow: wrap
    link-external-newwindow: true
```

The official UU logo files are on the
[corporate identity site](https://www.uu.nl/en/organisation/corporate-identity);
download the right variant rather than taking one off a web page.
